name: Taking in requests from anywhere
vision_statement: A person or a program reaches the runner from wherever they work, by a message, a terminal, a live channel or the package itself, and is understood the same way.
opportunities: A runner is reached from many places and each has its own failure and cost, which the parent solution measures one by one and none together: a short chat message must not pay for a long run, an image has to be described before it can ground an answer, input that arrives while a run works must be heard at the next decision, a terminal session needs helper calls that cost a fraction of a cent, and a developer needs a package that installs and runs on an empty environment, learned from documents and examples that are kept true.
solution_coherence: take-in-the-world lets a person or a program reach the runner from wherever they work and be understood the same way, and ways_in is its arm. route-a-message matches each message to the handling it needs, from a direct answer to a long run. describe-an-attachment turns an image the person attached into text that can ground the answer. feed-context-sources brings what changed in a work item since the last turn. receive-input-mid-run lets a person change direction or stop a run that is already working. operate-from-a-terminal runs the tools from the command line with predictable output and exit codes. assist-a-terminal-session makes the small model calls a terminal session needs. expose-the-public-api gives a program a stable package to import and configure. explain-qar documents the package through expose-the-public-api so that a newcomer can learn it from complete documents. learn-by-example shows how to use the package through expose-the-public-api in small examples that run on an empty environment. configure-a-lane gives whoever runs a lane one configuration, built from its file and its environment in a fixed order, so every lane is set up the same way.
